rubrics.justification: Provides a generally plausible blastocyst description with appropriate caveats, but partially conflicts with the lab-reported 3AA by calling it full to early-expanded and mentions possible debris/fragmentation not clearly established from a single image.
Thoroughly integrates age, ovarian reserve, BMI, endometriosis, semen parameters, endometrial thickness, lifestyle, and first-cycle status with embryo quality and prognosis.

Reasoning is logical and mostly consistent, with a clear link from embryo quality and patient factors to prognosis; only minor tension between image-based morphology comments and acceptance of the 3AA grade.

Recommendations are largely consistent with IVF practice guidelines, including SET for a good-prognosis young patient and cautious use of PGT-A; minor deductions for mentioning supplements/surgery options with limited evidence without stronger qualification.

Gives practical next steps for transfer management and contingency planning, including SET, luteal support, and further evaluation if unsuccessful, though some suggestions remain somewhat broad rather than protocol-specific.
